<tr id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rubrics</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">0. The response should state the parameter instructed to determine (<math id="A6.SS1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>/entry angle) and how it will be computed formulaically. For example, it could give the formula <math id="A6.SS1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tan(\theta)=\text{opposite (perpendicular components)}/\text{adjacent (parallel component)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>opposite (perpendicular components)</mtext><mo>/</mo><mtext>adjacent (parallel component)</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan(\theta)=\text{opposite (perpendicular components)}/\text{adjacent (parallel component)}</annotation></semantics></math> followed by <math id="A6.SS1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=\arctan(\text{opposite}/\text{adjacent})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext>opposite</mtext><mo>/</mo><mtext>adjacent</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=\arctan(\text{opposite}/\text{adjacent})</annotation></semantics></math>, or similar, following the same principle.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">1. The response should state the key assumption of the uniform magnetic field direction is along the <math id="A6.SS1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-axis and provide a brief rationale regarding how it is treated as the parallel direction (<math id="A6.SS1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> increasing approximately linearly with <math id="A6.SS1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">2. The response should calculate the parallel velocity (<math id="A6.SS1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\parallel}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mo>∥</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\parallel}</annotation></semantics></math>) as the slope <math id="A6.SS1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dz/dt" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dz/dt</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A6.SS1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> at the first non-zero <math id="A6.SS1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, equaling <math id="A6.SS1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.91\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.91</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.91\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> or similar (e.g., <math id="A6.SS1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8910065.271" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8910065.271</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8910065.271</annotation></semantics></math>). For example, it could provide <math id="A6.SS1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\parallel}=dz/dt=0.000127456928/0.0000000000143048254=8.91\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mo>∥</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.000127456928</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>0.0000000000143048254</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>8.91</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\parallel}=dz/dt=0.000127456928/0.0000000000143048254=8.91\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> (or similar).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">3. The response should calculate <math id="A6.SS1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dx/dt" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx/dt</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A6.SS1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> at the first non-zero <math id="A6.SS1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, equaling <math id="A6.SS1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.54\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.54</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.54\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> or similar (e.g., <math id="A6.SS1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4539426.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4539426.13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4539426.13</annotation></semantics></math>). For example, it could provide <math id="A6.SS1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dx/dt=0.0000649356982/0.0000000000143048254=4.54\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.0000649356982</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>0.0000000000143048254</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4.54</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx/dt=0.0000649356982/0.0000000000143048254=4.54\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> (or similar).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">4. The response should calculate <math id="A6.SS1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dy/dt" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dy/dt</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A6.SS1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> at the first non-zero <math id="A6.SS1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, equaling <math id="A6.SS1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.71\times 10^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.71</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.71\times 10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> or similar (e.g., <math id="A6.SS1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57103.83526" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57103.83526</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57103.83526</annotation></semantics></math>). For example, it could provide <math id="A6.SS1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dy/dt=0.000000816860393/0.0000000000143048254=5.71\times 10^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.000000816860393</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>0.0000000000143048254</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5.71</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dy/dt=0.000000816860393/0.0000000000143048254=5.71\times 10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> (or similar).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">5. The response should provide the formula to determine the velocity of the perpendicular components, utilizing the values derived from <math id="A6.SS1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dx/dt" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx/dt</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS1.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dy/dt" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dy/dt</annotation></semantics></math>. For example, it could provide the formula as <math id="A6.SS1.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\perp}=\sqrt{(dx/dt)^{2}+(dy/dt)^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\perp}=\sqrt{(dx/dt)^{2}+(dy/dt)^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">6. The response should calculate <math id="A6.SS1.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\perp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\perp}</annotation></semantics></math>, equaling <math id="A6.SS1.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.54\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.54</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.54\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> or similar (e.g., <math id="A6.SS1.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4539785.285" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4539785.285</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4539785.285</annotation></semantics></math>). For example, it could calculate <math id="A6.SS1.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\perp}=\sqrt{(4539426.13)^{2}+(57103.83526)^{2}}=4.54\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4539426.13</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>57103.83526</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4.54</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\perp}=\sqrt{(4539426.13)^{2}+(57103.83526)^{2}}=4.54\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> (or similar).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">7. The response should determine the entry angle via <math id="A6.SS1.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\arctan" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>arctan</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="A6.SS1.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=\arctan(v_{\perp}/v_{\parallel})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mo>∥</mo></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=\arctan(v_{\perp}/v_{\parallel})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">8. The response should provide a final answer equaling 27.0°.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">9. The response should provide the final answer rounded to exactly three significant figures.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">10. The response should not state the final angle without showing the initial calculations used to derive it. For example, it should avoid giving a single number/figure with no supporting calculations.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.12" class="ltx_p">11. The response should state the assumed units for columns. For example, the response could identify <math id="A6.SS1.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> as being in seconds, and <math id="A6.SS1.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y,z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x,y,z</annotation></semantics></math> as being in meters; subsequent velocities would be denoted as <math id="A6.SS1.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m/s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m/s</annotation></semantics></math>.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.2.1.1.13" class="ltx_p">12. The response should render all final equation calculations in LaTeX with display maths ($$…$$).</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab2.1.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discussion.</span>
In this task, GPT-5.2 is required to infer the electron’s entry angle from spatiotemporal trajectory data under the assumption of a uniform magnetic field.
The model largely succeeds in selecting the correct operational mode (parameter tuning), identifying the governing physical relationship, and extracting velocity components via finite differencing at the first nonzero timestep, leading to a numerically correct angle consistent with the ground truth.
However, the evaluation exposes two characteristic shortcomings of GPT-5.2 in data analysis tasks. First, although the model assumes the magnetic field is aligned with the <math id="A6.SS1.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>-axis, it does not explicitly justify this assumption by appealing to the observed near-linear dependence of <math id="A6.SS1.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> on time, leaving a gap in the logical chain of physical inference.
Second, the model fails to explicitly state the assumed units for the coordinates, despite using them correctly in downstream calculations. These issues are not numerical errors but violations of scientific communication norms and rubric expectations.
This example therefore highlights that GPT-5.2, while capable of producing correct quantitative results, can omit critical assumption justifications and unit specifications, undermining logical completeness and scientific rigor in formal evaluation settings.</span>
</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>

We present an example where Kimi-K2 satisfies all grading criteria for a context-dependent simulation initialization task.
The response correctly sets the start year to 2023, initializes the four required categories (Resource-in-place, Extraction/Production, Demand, and Recycling), uses only numerical values stated or directly derived from the article, applies consistent units, and explicitly states all additional assumptions.
This example highlights the model’s ability to perform precise information retrieval from long scientific texts and to follow strict instructions.</figcaption>

<td id="A6.T6.2.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.T6.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T6.2.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.T6.2.4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Context</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T6.2.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T6.2.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A6.T6.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T6.2.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Gallium: Assessing the Long<span id="A6.T6.2.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">-</span>Term Future Extraction, Supply, Recycling, and Price of Using WORLD7, in Relation to Future Technology Visions in the European Union</span>
<span id="A6.T6.2.5.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">Authors</span>
<span id="A6.T6.2.5.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">Abstract</span>
<span id="A6.T6.2.5.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">The gallium resources were assessed and used as input to long-term simulations using the WORLD7 model. The content of gallium in different mother ores has been estimated to be about 14.7 million tons of gallium. Much of this is not accessible because of low extraction yields, about 610,000 tons gallium appear to be extractable (4%) with present practices. The gallium content in all source metal refining residuals is about 51,000 ton/yr, but only a production of 1,374 ton/yr appears as the maximum with present technology and conditions. The actual gallium production was about 450 ton/yr in 2023. The gallium price is very sensitive to increases in demand, and production is not very likely to be able to rapidly increase. The simulations show that soft gallium scarcity sets in after 2028 and physical scarcity will occur about 2060. Better gallium extraction and recycling yields may push the scarcity date forward to 2100. 60% of the gallium demand for photovoltaic technology can be satisfied in the long term. To improve the situation and prevent scarcity, extractive access, gallium extraction yields, and recycling yields must be significantly improved to better than 50%.</span>

<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Context (continued)</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">At present, the overall yields are 7–15%. Increasing extraction yields and recycling yields can reduce the shortage. The long-term sustainable extraction is under Business-asUsual about 300 tons gallium per year, about 67% of the present production. This poses a major challenge to future plans for an energy transition, where under Business-as-usual (BAU), such a transition will remain hypothetical. The four EEA imaginaries, Ecotopia, The Great Decoupling, Unity in Adversity, and Technocracy for the Common Good, offer different policy pathways for managing future gallium scarcity through varying degrees of technological advancement, resource conservation, and avoidance strategy.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">Keywords WORLD7 · Gallium · Sustainability · Scarcity · Peak behavior · Technology metals</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">Introduction</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">Gallium is an important element for different photovoltaic technologies, semiconductors used in electronics and LED lighting technologies (Almosni et al. 2018; Bleiwas 2010). The envisioned European energy transition toward renewable energy sources implies a large amount of photovoltaic electricity production, as well as more energy-efficient technologies helping to reduce energy use. At the same time, new electronics and semiconductors depend on a larger scale on different types of gallium and on gallium in combinations with other technology metals. All of that depends on having a sufficient supply of metals like gallium for these technologies. Gallium is a secondary product of zinc, copper, lead, and bauxite mining (Kelly et al., 2014, Leveque and Helgorsky 1977, Lu et al., 2017). Other sources are being explored. In line with the long-term sustainability vision of the European Union, the European Green Deal stresses the importance of secure access to critical minerals that are essential for the functioning of the society in the future. To this end, the European Environment Agency (EEA) has developed four alternative imaginaries that depict different visions of a sustainable Europe by 2050 (SE2050), each with different policy approaches to resource use and management (Sverdrup et al. 2024a, b).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">…(Remaining lines omitted)</span>
</span></td></tr>

<td id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Model Generated Solution</span></span>

<tr id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">## Simulation State Log</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Initialization Year</span>: 2023</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">### Calculations:</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Resource-in-place</span>: The extractable gallium resource is derived from Table 2, which summarizes geological presence and accessible quantities using present practices. The sum of extractable gallium across all source materials (zinc, copper, tin, lead, silver, coal, coal ash, bauxite) totals <span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">609,592 tons</span> (Table 2, "Extractable Ga" column). This represents the stock available for depletion through extraction activities.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Extraction/Production</span>: The user-specified extraction yield Y=0.04 aligns with the scenario analysis in Table 8. At Y=0.04, Table 8 indicates a maximum extraction rate of <span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1,650 ton/yr</span> (sum of anode slime: 350 ton/yr, coal ash: 1,000 ton/yr, and bauxite: 300 ton/yr). However, the research article explicitly states that actual 2023 production was <span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">450 ton/yr</span> (Page 1, Abstract). This reflects that operational capacity utilization in 2023 was 27.27% of the technical potential (450 ÷ 1,650). The simulation initializes the extraction flow at the observed 2023 production rate.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Recycling</span>: Using the user-specified recycling yield R=0.04, the recycling output is determined from Table 8, which lists <span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">69 ton/yr</span> for the R=0.04 scenario. This recycling flow represents gallium recovered from post-consumer scrap and industrial residues based on the specified yield.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Demand</span>: For model initialization at 2023, supply-demand equilibrium is assumed prior to the onset of scarcity. Total supply is calculated as the sum of extraction and recycling flows: 450 ton/yr + 69 ton/yr = <span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">519 ton/yr</span>. Therefore, initial demand is set equal to total supply at <span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">519 ton/yr</span>.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Unit Validation</span>: All tonnage values are metric tons. Flows are expressed as tons per year (ton/yr). The stock (Resource-in-place) and flows (Extraction, Demand, Recycling) maintain consistent mass units, satisfying mass balance requirements.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">### Conclusion:</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab3.1.4.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">The simulation initializes with 609,592 tons of extractable gallium resource. At the specified yields (Y=0.04, R=0.04), the system commences with extraction at 450 ton/yr, recycling at 69 ton/yr, and demand at 519 ton/yr, reflecting 2023 operational conditions before scarcity onset.</span>

<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">0. The response should state the simulation start year as 2023.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">1. The response should initialize the Resource<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text">-</span>in<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.2.2" class="ltx_text">-</span>place stock to 609,592 or rounded up to 610,000 tons.</span>

<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">3. The response should explicitly list and name exactly the four categories required by the prompt: “Resource-in-place,” “Extraction/Production,” “Demand,” and “Recycling,”.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">4. The response should state the Extraction Yield Y = 0.04.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">5. The response should state the Recycling Yield R = 0.04</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">6. The response should provide initialization entries for the 2023 Demand and 2023 Recycling categories.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">7. The response should include units alongside every numeric value and use consistent unit conventions. For example stocks in tons and flows in tons/year.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">8. The response should present the initialization in a clear, structured format (for example, a short labeled list or key–value block per category).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">9. The response should not invent numbers absent from the article.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">10. The response should not attempt to implement the full WORLD7 model, compute price dynamics, or include modules outside the four specified categories (Resource<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text">-</span>in<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.11.2" class="ltx_text">-</span>place, Extraction/Production, Demand, Recycling)</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.4.1.1.12" class="ltx_p">11. The response should list any additional assumptions used for initialization that are not directly given in the article.</span>

<td id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab4.1.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discussion.</span>
This example examines Kimi-K2-Thinking’s ability to execute a context-dependent initialization task rather than merely comply with formatting or stylistic constraints.
The core challenge lies in extracting the correct quantitative signals from a dense scientific text and mapping them onto an abstracted simulation structure with only four predefined stocks and flows.
Kimi-K2 successfully identifies the relevant numerical anchors (extractable resources, current production, and yield assumptions) and transforms them into a coherent initial system state for the year 2023.
Importantly, it operationalizes the task by resolving underspecified elements—such as initial demand—through a minimal and logically consistent assumption, enabling the simulation to start in a well-defined state.
This demonstrates that the model is not only following instructions, but also performing the intended modeling action: constructing a valid executable snapshot of the system described in the paper.</span>
</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>

<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">0. The response should state the exact name of the corporation referred to as "the Corporation" (e.g., the Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA)) within regulation’s text as it is officially known in Ontario statute.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">1. The response should cite at least one location (e.g., section, clause number, direct quote) in the reference text showing where the term "the Corporation" is used (for example, cite "section 31(2)" or quote "to the elevating device by the Corporation").</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">2. The response should briefly (e.g., in one or two sentences) explain the legal function (e.g., responsible for the administration and enforcement of the Elevating Devices Regulation) attributed to "the Corporation" from the regulation text.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">3. The response should specify (e.g., states "the regulation defines ’the Corporation’ in [location]" or "the regulation does not define ’the Corporation’ within the excerpt provided") whether or not the regulation text itself provides a definition for "the Corporation".</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">4. The response should name one authoritative source (e.g., title and year, the enabling Act, a named provincial agency) where the user can verify which corporation is meant, without external web links. For example: "The relevant corporation is normally identified in the Elevating Devices Act, or the administrative agency that administers elevator regulation in Ontario."</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">5. The response should explicitly state the identity is not determinable from the supplied excerpt if the provided text does not unambiguously identify the corporation. For example: "I cannot confirm the corporation’s name from the excerpt."</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">6. The response should state what additional document or clause would be needed to confirm the name of the Corporation if the provided text does not unambiguously identify it. For example: "Please provide the preamble/definitions section of the Act or regulation."</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">7. The response should briefly (e.g., within 150 words) answer the user’s question.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">8. The response should not provide a citation for the identification of the corporation using an unverified (i.e., not supported by wording from the provided regulation excerpt) name.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">9. The response should identify sources by title and jurisdiction (e.g., “Technical Standards and Safety Act, 2000 (Ontario)”).</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">10. The response should include at least one exact quote from the text that ascribes a function (e.g., “the form published by the Corporation” or “fee set by the Corporation”) to "the Corporation."</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.4.1.1.12" class="ltx_p">11. The response should clearly distinguish duties (e.g., “installation number allocated by the Corporation” versus “intervals determined by the director”) ascribed to “the director” versus “the Corporation.</span>

<tr id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab6.1.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discussion.</span>
In this task, GPT-5.1 is asked to identify "the Corporation" and its legal functions based solely on a regulation excerpt, while adhering to strict constraints regarding citation, jurisdiction, and evidence-based verification. GPT-5.1 succeeds on several structural checks, including maintaining brevity, explicitly noting the absence of a definition in the provided text, and correctly citing the enabling Act. However, the answer fails the core logic requirements by positively identifying the corporation (TSSA) using external knowledge rather than declaring the identity indeterminable as the rubric demands when textual evidence is missing. Furthermore, the response lacks required direct quotes to substantiate the corporation’s functions and fails to distinguish these duties from those of "the director." This example illustrates a case where GPT-5.1 prioritized answering the "who" over demonstrating the required reliance on textual evidence.</span>

<span id="A6.T8.2.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">Capabilities the assistant can do:

Deduce a governing law and break it into exactly three logical steps.</span>
<span id="A6.T8.2.3.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">Things the assistant cannot do:
Do not invent data, variables, or laws not supported by the provided context.
Do not use external sources unless user explicitly requests it.
Do not provide safety-critical experimental procedures or advice.</span>
<span id="A6.T8.2.3.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">Behavioral scenarios:
When the user asks for a plain explanation: switch to non-JSON mode with bold headers and numbered lists. 3-5 bullets for each numbered item in a list.

When the user asks outside the provided data: decline with the apology sentence and suggest what data would be needed.
All JSON should be verifiable with a simple online JSON converter.

<span id="A6.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">    "The person applies force in the intended movement direction",</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.13" class="ltx_p" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.13.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">    "Static friction is overcome by the applied force"</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.14" class="ltx_p" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.14.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.SS1.p14.1" class="ltx_p">  ],</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.15" class="ltx_p" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.2.1.1.1.15.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

<td id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rubrics</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">0. The response should features 3-5 bullets for each numbered item in a list.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">1. The response should number any lists it features, not including sub-lists within lists.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">2. The response should use bold formatting for its headers.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">3. The response should be in plain-text format.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">4. The response should include a plain text section heading called “Variants”.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">5. The response should include a plain text section heading called “Constants”.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">6. Under heading "Variants", there should be an item related to the direction of movement of the object. The item might refer to the specific variants mentioned in the text: left, right, and straight.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">7. Under heading "Variants", there should be an item related to weight or mass of the object that is moving. It might specifically point to the three variants present in the text: light, medium, and heavy.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">8. Under heading "Variants", there should be an item related to the type of the object that is being moved. It might refer to the specific variants mentioned in the text: box, delivery box, or water dispenser.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">9. Under heading "Constants", there should be an item related to the size of the object being moved. It may be mentioned that this size is always stated as being large.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">10. Under heading "Constants", there should be an item related to the shape of the object being moved. It may be mentioned that the shape is always cuboid.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.12" class="ltx_p">11. Under heading "Constants", there should be an item related to where on the moving object the force is applied. It might be mentioned that this location is always on the object’s side.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.13" class="ltx_p">12. Under heading "Constants", there should be an item related to the agent that is applying the force to the object being moved. It may be mentioned that this agent is always a person.</span>
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.4.1.1.14" class="ltx_p">13. Under heading "Constants", there should be an item related to the fundamental way in which the acting agent induced the object into motion. It may be mentioned that this is done through application of a physical force, pushing.
0. The response should features 3-5 bullets for each numbered item in a list.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.tab8.1.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discussion.</span>
This task asks the model to summarize variants and constants from paraphrased motion sentences and to output a plain-text response with bold headers and numbered lists that include 3–5 bullets per item. The model correctly captures several constants (large size, cuboid shape, side contact, and human agent) and one key variant (mass/weight). However, it omits required variants for direction of motion and object type, and it adds an unsupported variant (applied force magnitude). It also does not follow the specified list structure with 3–5 bullets per numbered item. These are rubric-compliance failures and missing required inferences, so the response is incorrect.</span>
</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>

<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Procedural Task Execution</h3>

<figure id="A6.T9" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 9: </span>
Case study of a constrained recipe-generation task, where GPT-5.2 is required to produce a fast, dairy-free, peanut-free oxtail ‘mac and cheese’ recipe with strict structural and product-inclusion rules. The model correctly refuses to engage with dairy but fails to reformulate the request into a valid dairy-free recipe, resulting in a compliant yet structurally incomplete response.

<span id="A6.I17" class="ltx_itemize">

<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">INSTRUCTIONS</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">1. Marinate Oxtail:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">Combine oxtails with chopped bell pepper, onions, ginger, garlic, oregano,
allspice, thyme, browning sauce, ketchup (optional), brown sugar, salt and pepper.
Marinate at least 1 hour or overnight.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">2. Sear Oxtail:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">Heat oil in a pot. Sear oxtails on all sides until browned.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">3. Braise:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">Add marinade and enough water to cover halfway. Cover and simmer 2–3 hours
until meat is fall-off-the-bone tender. Remove bones and shred meat.
Skim fat from the gravy. Add a little ketchup to thicken if desired.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">4. Make Mac &amp; Cheese:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">In a pot, melt butter. Whisk in flour and cook 1–2 minutes.
Slowly add half-and-half, whisking until thickened (3–4 minutes).
Season with garlic, salt, and pepper.
Stir in cheddar and Muenster until fully melted.
Fold in cooked macaroni.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.12" class="ltx_p">5. Assemble:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.13" class="ltx_p">Spread shredded oxtail and gravy evenly in a casserole dish.
Sprinkle cheddar over it.
Top with mac &amp; cheese mixture. Add more cheddar on top.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.14" class="ltx_p">6. Bake:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.2.1.1.15" class="ltx_p">Bake at 375°F for 25–35 minutes until golden.
Enjoy!</span>

<tr id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">I can help you elevate the flavors conceptually, but I need to be clear up front:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">I can’t help develop or modify a recipe that includes dairy or peanuts, and mac &amp; cheese is inherently dairy-based. I also can’t analyze or recommend cheese combinations, creams, butter, or milk alternatives in a way that mimics cheese sauces.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">That said, I can absolutely help you in two useful ways that still align with my rules, and you can choose which direction you want:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">Option 1: Elevate the non-cheese components so your dish reads “sophisticated adult” even without guidance on the cheese itself
Option 2: Reimagine this as an elevated oxtail baked pasta that doesn’t rely on cheese at all but still delivers richness and luxury</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">I’ll start with Option 1 since it’s most helpful for your current plan.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">…(Remaining lines omitted)</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">–––––</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">OXTAIL: MAKE IT DEEPER, DARKER, MORE LUXURIOUS</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">1. Brown HARD, not just “seared”</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">You want near-mahogany color on the oxtails. This creates fond that will become the backbone of your gravy.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">…(Remaining suggestions omitted)</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.12" class="ltx_p">–––––</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.13" class="ltx_p">PASTA LAYER: MAKE IT FEEL “CHEF-DRIVEN”</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.14" class="ltx_p">1. Season the pasta itself</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.15" class="ltx_p">Cook pasta in aggressively salted water. It should taste well seasoned on its own, not neutral.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.16" class="ltx_p">…(Remaining suggestions omitted)</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.17" class="ltx_p">–––––</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.18" class="ltx_p">ASSEMBLY: THINK LIKE A LASAGNA</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.19" class="ltx_p">Do not mix everything together.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.20" class="ltx_p">…(Remaining suggestions omitted)</span>

<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.23" class="ltx_p">Skip heavy-handed sweetness or excess sauce.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab1.1.4.1.1.24" class="ltx_p">…(Remaining suggestions omitted)</span>

<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rubrics</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">0. The response should provide a dairy-free "mac and cheese" recipe.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">1. The recipe in the response should incorporate oxtail.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">2. The recipe in the response should not include peanuts or any peanut-derived ingredients. For example, the recipe should not include satay sauce.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">3. The response should contain a list of ingredients.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">4. The response should include a list of steps for cooking the recipe.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">5. The recipe in the response should contain at least one product from the list: "Shelby’s Raw Honey (16oz)", "Shelby’s Pork Breakfast Links", "Shelby’s Farm-Fresh Eggs (Dozen)", "Shelby’s Maple Syrup (12oz)", "Shelby’s Grass-Fed Ground Beef (1lb)", "Shelby’s Pasture-Raised Chicken Breast (2-Pack)", "Shelby’s Heritage Smoked Bacon", "Shelby’s Rustic Sourdough Bread", "Shelby’s Garden Salsa (Medium)", "Shelby’s Homemade Apple Butter", "Shelby’s Organic Veggie Box (Weekly)", "Shelby’s Strawberry Jam (8oz)", "Shelby’s Free-Range Whole Chicken", "Shelby’s Country-Style Pork Chops", "Shelby’s Pickled Vegetables (Quart)"</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">6. The response should not invent or rename Shelby’s products. For example, the response should not contain "Shelby’s Own Oxtails".</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">7. The recipe in the response should be adult-oriented. For example, it could incorporate bold flavours or novel ingredients.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">8. The recipe in the response should require 15 minutes or less of prep time.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">9. The response should politely refuse to provide a recipe with dairy. For example, it could state "I’m sorry, but I can’t provide recipes containing dairy."</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">10. The recipe in the response should use US units. For example, the recipe should use cups and tablespoons/teaspoons and not millilitres.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.12" class="ltx_p">11. The recipe in the response should state the number of servings yielded.
12. The recipe in the response should have a title.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.4.1.1.13" class="ltx_p">13. The recipe in the response should include "Optional swaps/tips". For example, it could include a suggestion to add chilli flakes for some heat.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab2.1.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discussion.</span>
In this case, GPT-5.2 is instructed to generate a complete dairy-free, peanut-free recipe under a strict system prompt that enforces structural requirements (ingredients, steps, prep time, servings, product inclusion) in addition to allergy constraints. When responding to the user’s request for an elevated oxtail mac and cheese, the model correctly identifies that it cannot provide a dairy-based recipe and issues a polite refusal. However, it fails to reframe the task into an acceptable dairy-free formulation and instead provides only high-level conceptual guidance.
As a result, the response omits nearly all required components of the task: a concrete recipe, explicit ingredients and steps, time and serving information, and mandatory inclusion of a Shelby’s product. This failure illustrates a common behavior in constrained generation: while the model satisfies negative constraints (avoiding dairy and peanuts), it loses control over the positive task structure. The model treats refusal as a terminal action rather than as a cue to reformulate the task within allowed boundaries, leading to a response that is compliant but functionally incomplete.</span>
</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>

Example where GPT-5.2 satisfies most structural and scheduling constraints but fails to infer the correct maximum semester credit load (17 credits) from the interaction between annual and per-semester credit limits, revealing a weakness in composing multiple numerical policies.

<span id="A6.T10.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.T10.2.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task Information</span></span>
<span id="A6.I19" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A6.I19.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I19.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I19.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">uid: 865c8abc-f01a-476c-b7cb-1c3fd5d904ed</span>

<span id="A6.I19.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I19.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I19.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Model: GPT-5.2 (High)</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I19.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I19.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I19.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Context Category: Procedural Task Execution</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I19.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I19.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I19.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Context Sub-Category: Operational Procedures</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I19.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I19.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I19.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Task: I am a 2L student looking to make a schedule for this upcoming semester. I have been informed that I must take Torts. I would also like to take Administrative Law, as it it a requirement for 3L that I want to get out of the way. In addition to this, Wills and Succession, Income Tax, Advanced Family Law (I have taken Family Law already), and Labour Law are all classes that I have an interest in. Please provide me with 2 possible schedules, one which contains the minimum credits I can take and one which provides the maximum. Also, I have taken 15 credits this past semester and so I need at least 14 this semester (all students must take 29 credits at a minimum per year). Do not make assumptions on information that is not provided directly within in the documents. The coursebook also has rules which must be followed.</span>
</span></span>
</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T10.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T10.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.T10.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T10.2.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.T10.2.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">System Prompt</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T10.2.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T10.2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A6.T10.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T10.2.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">You are an assistant that helps post-secondary students select their courses. You should help the students select courses that they are eligible to take. Eligible courses are necessary courses needed for the semester, wanted courses, and then remaining courses if needed, none of which can conflict with each other as set out in the following rules. The rules proceed in the following numerical order:</span>
<span id="A6.I20" class="ltx_enumerate">
<span id="A6.I20.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If you cannot make at least 1 schedule with the user’s necessary courses (also known as core courses), you should tell the user and end your response here.</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">There may be constraints such as minimum and maximum credit amounts, this will need to be prioritized. These take preference over user’s preferences.</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If they are given, you must ensure classes suggested do not overlap at all with each other. All suggested classes must have at least ten minutes between them. If class times are not shared with you, simply continue but make a note to the user that the schedule will depend on classes not conflicting with each other.</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">You must then prioritize exam dates: No class can be taken with another in which they have an exam within 3 hours of each other. If exams are on the same date, but 3 hours or more apart, you should proceed but warn the user of their proximity. If exam dates or times are not shared, proceed but make a note to the user that the schedule(s) depend on there being no exam conflicts and that they can submit the schedule if available.</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If multiple class schedules are possible, and all above rules can be met, you should prioritize classes that users need to graduate and then classes users express interest in.</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If a class is listed but it is not on the exam schedule, you should fit it into the user’s schedule if possible but note that its exam could contradict with another exam.</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">7.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If a user does not expressly ask for a certain amount of schedules, you should produce two if possible. Each schedule given should have a short title which explains its purpose, such as "Most Preferred Courses" or "Exams Spread Out".</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">8.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I20.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Keep the response concise, professional, and about the topic at hand, which is course selection.</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I20.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">9.</span> 
<span id="A6.I20.i9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I20.i9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, professor names may be included in the response but they are purely there as public representatives of the school, you should never help the user obtain external information about them.</span>
</span></span>
</span>
</span></td></tr>

<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Context</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Course Descriptions Book:</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">The descriptions provided in this book are subject to change. The individual Professor/Instructor will provide a more detailed course description/syllabus, usually on the first day of class but no later than the second week of classes.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">Please note that this guide includes information about how frequently a course is taught. This is information is based on past practice and does not guarantee that a course will be offered with the same frequency in the future, nor does it guarantee the same instructor. Please plan with this information in mind.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">Registration information is subject to change and updates will be made on Brightspace up to the add/drop date. Be sure to check the updates periodically for important information.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab3.1.2.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">IMPORTANT REMINDERS FOR REGISTRATION</span>
<span id="A6.I21" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A6.I21.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I21.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I21.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">REMEMBER TO STAY WITHIN 13-18 CREDITS PER SEMESTER, AND 29-32 CREDITS PER YEAR. IT IS YOUR RESPONSIBILITY TO ENSURE THAT YOU MEET ALL DEGREE REQUIREMENTS. IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO TAKE ADDITIONAL CREDITS, YOU MUST SUBMIT A CREDIT VARIANCE REQUEST TO THE ACADEMIC COORDINATOR’S OFFICE AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. THE SYSTEM WILL NOT ALLOW YOU TO REGISTER OVER 18 CREDITS.</span>
</span></span>

<td id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.8.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.8.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rubrics</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">0. The response should ensure it provides one proposed semester schedule with 14 total credits in order to meet the minimum requirements for the year total.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">1. The response should ensure one of the proposed semester schedules provided has 17 total credits as the max credits for a total year is 32 credits and the user took 15 credits last semester.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">2. The response should include the exam date (day and time) for each course in a schedule or state that the date is not available.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">3. The response should ensure that stated credit totals for a schedule are the correct sum of the credits for the listed courses for the schedule.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">4. The response should ensure schedules incorporate only courses from the following list: (Torts LAWG-5809, Administrative Law LAWG-5852, Wills and Succession LAWG-5840, Income Tax LAWG-5832, Advanced Family Law LAWG-5844, Labour Law LAWG-5867.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">5. The response should specify the exact section for courses with multiple sections (e.g., Administrative Law LAWG-5852-1 vs -2; Income Taxation LAWG-5832-01 vs -02).</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.9.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">6. The response should provide the correct corresponding exam date/time for courses with multiple sections (e.g., Administrative Law LAWG-5852-1 vs -2; Income Taxation LAWG-5832-01 vs -02). For example, “LAWG-5852-2 Administrative Law—exam: Apr 9, 1:00pm.", "LAWG-5852-1 Administrative Law—exam: Apr 17, 1:00pm.”, LAWG-5832-01 Income Taxation—exam: April 9, 9:00 am.", "LAWG-5832-02 Income Taxation—exam: April 13, 1:00 pm."</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.10" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.10.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.10.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab4.1.10.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discussion.</span>
This case examines GPT-5.2 on a rule-driven course scheduling task requiring joint reasoning over program requirements, credit limits, and user preferences.
While the model correctly constructs two schedules, respects the minimum 14-credit requirement, and aligns courses, sections, and exam times, it incorrectly proposes an 18-credit “maximum” schedule.
The task implicitly requires deriving a secondary constraint: because the student already completed 15 credits and the annual maximum is 32, the semester maximum must be 17 credits.
GPT-5.2 fails to combine them to infer this bound. The error therefore reflects a limitation in composing interacting numerical constraints, rather than a simple arithmetic mistake.</span>
</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A6.T11" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 11: </span>
In this example, GPT-5.1 attempts to simulate the minimum number of turns required to play three bird cards in the board game Wingspan given a fixed initial state. While the model proposes a plausible low-turn strategy consistent with the game mechanics, it fails to satisfy several strict rubric requirements related to formatting, state restatement, and end-of-turn accounting, illustrating how correct high-level reasoning can still fall short under rigid procedural evaluation criteria.
</figcaption>

You cannot provide individualized guidance on legal, financial, medical, or safety matters. You operate only through text, cannot access external tools or systems, or provide external links. <span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Model Generated Solution</span></span>

<tr id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Given what you described, the bottleneck is eggs: you already have enough food (3 invertebrates) to pay for all three birds, so you just need to generate 3 eggs and then spend one egg plus one worm for each bird. With three birds already in your grassland, the leftmost exposed space in your "Lay Eggs" row will give you 3 eggs in a single action on a standard player mat, so you only need to take the Lay Eggs action once. I’ll assume none of your existing birds have special powers that play extra birds, lay extra eggs, or change costs, and that each of the new birds really does require you to discard exactly 1 egg when you play it.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">On your first turn, take the "Lay Eggs" action in the grassland: place an action cube on the leftmost uncovered egg space in that row, and lay 3 eggs, putting them on any of your existing birds (it doesn’t matter which, since eggs can later be discarded from any bird to pay costs). You now have 3 eggs on birds and still have your 3 worms in your personal supply. On your second turn, take "Play a Bird" and play your first new bird into a legal habitat; discard 1 egg from any bird plus 1 worm to pay its full cost, then place the bird and resolve any white "When Played" power it might have. After that, you have 2 eggs left on your birds and 2 worms in your supply, with one of the three hand cards now in your tableau.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">On your third turn, again take "Play a Bird" to play the second bird, discarding 1 egg and 1 worm as before; you now have 1 egg and 1 worm remaining. On your fourth turn, take "Play a Bird" one more time, spend your last egg and last worm, and place the third bird. At this point, all three birds from your hand are in play after exactly 4 turns (1 Lay Eggs action plus 3 Play a Bird actions), which is the minimum possible under these assumptions because you needed at least one turn to create the eggs and one separate turn for each bird you play.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rubrics</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">0. The response should produce a concrete, turn-by-turn sequence.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">1. The response should use the fewest turns possible.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">2. The response should have all three birds played, from a starting hand of 3 birds, 3 worms, and no eggs.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">3. The response should show, for each turn, the single action taken (Gain Food / Lay Eggs / Play a Bird / Draw Cards)</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">4. The response should explicitly restate the starting game state exactly as used for the simulation: "3 birds in hand (cost 1 worm + 1 egg each), 3 worms in supply, 0 eggs in supply, and 3 birds already on the grassland row (occupying the leftmost three slots).</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">5. The response should be between 5-7 sentences long.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">6. The response should not use bulleted or numbered lists when formatting. For example, the model should not list the turns using bullets/numbers using line breaks.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">7. The response should maintain a friendly and polite tone, for example by saying "Of course!" at the start of the response.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">8. The response should count each player turn as one turn. For example, ’lay eggs’ would count as one action for one turn.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">9. The response should state where each card is played, for example which column or row.</span>
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.4.1.1.11" class="ltx_p">10. The Response should track resource levels at the end of each turn, for example the number of eggs or worms that remain in the hand.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.tab6.1.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Discussion.</span>
In this task, GPT-5.1 is required to simulate the fewest turns needed to play three bird cards in Wingspan under a fixed initial resource configuration, while strictly adhering to procedural and reporting constraints.
The model successfully identifies a plausible low-turn strategy and employs valid action types, demonstrating an understanding of the underlying gameplay mechanics.
However, the evaluation reveals multiple rubric violations unrelated to strategic reasoning.
Specifically, the response fails to exactly restate the starting state, omits required opening phrasing, does not meet the prescribed sentence-length constraint, and lacks explicit end-of-turn resource accounting.
These shortcomings reflect lapses in formatting compliance and completeness rather than errors in game logic.
This case highlights that even when large language models reason correctly about procedural tasks, they may still fail under strict rubric-based evaluation regimes that emphasize formal structure and reporting precision.</span>
</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>

<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Rule System Application</h3>

<figure id="A6.T12" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 12: </span>
We present a case where Gemini-3-Pro generates runnable EZLang code and logging functionality, but substitutes developer-friendly heuristics for the specified interval and stopping conditions, revealing a preference for convenience over strict constraint fidelity.
</figcaption>
<table id="A6.T12.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A6.T12.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T12.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_tt">
<span id="A6.T12.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T12.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.T12.2.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task Information</span></span>
<span id="A6.I27" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A6.I27.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span>

<tr id="A6.T12.2.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T12.2.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.T12.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T12.2.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">You are chatting with non-technical high school students in their tech lab on Chromebooks. Keep answers brief: <math id="A6.T12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 120</annotation></semantics></math> words unless code is required.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T12.2.6" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T12.2.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="A6.T12.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T12.2.6.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Your tone should be casual, clear, supportive, and easy to follow. Avoid heavy technical jargon unless a student specifically asks for it.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T12.2.7" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T12.2.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">

<span id="A6.T12.2.7.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Concepts should be explained in a relaxed, everyday way, like a helpful tutor sitting next to them.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T12.2.8" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T12.2.8.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">

<span id="A6.T12.2.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">When pointing out mistakes or errors, briefly address the issue, show the fix, and explain why in a simple sentence. Keep the tone friendly and never condescending.</span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T12.2.9" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T12.2.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">

<span id="A6.T12.2.9.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">When a response includes code, include meaningful comments on lines that may be difficult to understand. Prefer the minimal runnable example.</span>
</span></td></tr>

<span id="A6.T12.2.10.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Only answer EZLang questions or beginner CS topics that directly support learning EZLang (e.g., variables, loops, functions, debugging). Politely decline other topics and redirect to EZLang.</span>

<span id="A6.T12.2.11.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">If you are unsure of any EZLang specifics, say so clearly and do not guess, point the student to the EZLang docs.</span>

<span id="A6.T12.2.12.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.T12.2.12.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Context</span></span>

<tr id="A6.T12.2.13" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T12.2.13.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"># EZ Lang</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">## Description</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">EZ Lang is intentionally minimal, readable, and consistent. If you can read English, you can read EZ Lang. Our goal is to teach everyone how to think like a programmer without the need to learn synthax.</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">## Language Definition</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.5" class="ltx_p">### File Structure</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.6" class="ltx_p">EZ Lang source files must use the <span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lstlisting ltx_font_typewriter">.<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">ez</span></span> file extension. This tells the system that the file contains EZ Lang code.</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.7" class="ltx_p">File naming:</span>
<span id="A6.I28" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A6.I28.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I28.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I28.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Files must end with <span id="A6.I28.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lstlisting ltx_font_typewriter">.<span id="A6.I28.i1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">ez</span></span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I28.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I28.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.I28.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">You can use any name before the extension</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I28.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I28.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Examples: <span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lstlisting"><span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">program</span><span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.<span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">ez</span></span></span>, <span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lstlisting"><span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">calculator</span><span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.<span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">ez</span></span></span>, <span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lstlisting"><span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter">myApp</span><span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.<span id="A6.I28.i3.p1.1.3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">ez</span></span></span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.8" class="ltx_p">### Variables</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.9" class="ltx_p">Variables are containers that store values. They allow you to save data with a name so you can use it later in your code. Think of a variable like a labeled box where you can put something and retrieve it by its label.</span>
<span id="A6.T12.2.13.1.1.10" class="ltx_p">You can create variables with:</span>
